title: Private: audit log events for upgrade/rollback actions
author: Benji Okafor
release_notes: - Private deployments: upgrade/rollback actions now emit audit log events with actor + timestamps + from/to versions (where known) and upgrade correlation id.
description: Summary: Add first-class audit log events for Redwood Private upgrade/rollback workflows so customers and Support can answer “who did what, when, and to which version” across VPC and on-prem deployments. This is part of the Private upgrade + rollback mechanism work and is a prerequisite for GA (security + supportability). Motivation/context: Today, upgrade runs emit operational logs and metrics, but the security/audit surface is incomplete. Enterprise customers (and our own Security review) require immutable, queryable audit records for change actions including upgrade start/abort/complete and rollback start/abort/complete. Design: We introduce a small, versioned set of audit event types emitted by the control plane when it receives/executes upgrade actions (API-triggered) and when it triggers an automated rollback (policy-triggered). Events are emitted to the existing audit pipeline with a stable schema and strict redaction (no secrets, no raw bundle contents). Each event includes: actor (user/service), actor_type, request_id, upgrade_correlation_id (if available), deployment_id, environment (vpc|onprem), from_version (best-effort), to_version (best-effort), outcome, and an optional failure_category (non-sensitive enum). Event types added: private.upgrade.plan_generated, private.upgrade.started, private.upgrade.completed, private.upgrade.aborted, private.rollback.started, private.rollback.completed, private.rollback.aborted. For automated rollbacks, actor_type=system and actor=redwood-control-plane; we also include triggered_by_event_id referencing the upgrade event that caused rollback. Implementation details: (1) Control plane upgrade API handlers now call audit.Record(...) after authZ succeeds and before enqueueing the upgrade job; completion/abort events are emitted from the job runner with final status and resolved versions. (2) Upgrade/rollback version fields are sourced from the control plane “desired version” state and the deployment component version report (fallback), to avoid trusting installer-supplied strings. (3) We propagate the existing request_id into the job context and attach upgrade_correlation_id if present from the installer. (4) Added unit tests for schema shape + redaction, and integration-ish tests for event emission ordering using the in-memory audit sink. Security notes: No secrets, tokens, or KMS key identifiers are logged. Bundle manifests are not embedded; only the bundle version/tag is recorded (when available). Failure reasons are mapped to a bounded enum (e.g., SCHEMA_FORWARD_ONLY, SNAPSHOT_PERMISSION_DENIED, HEALTH_GATE_TIMEOUT) to avoid leaking infrastructure details. Test plan: - go test ./... (control plane) - Added tests: TestUpgradeAuditEvents_ApiTriggered, TestRollbackAuditEvents_SystemTriggered, TestAuditEvent_Redaction - Manual: ran upgrade in staging private env and verified events in audit index via internal dashboard query (see comment). Rollout: This is control-plane-only; installer/helm changes are not required. Existing audit consumers can ignore unknown event_type values; schema version field included for forward compatibility.
commits: control-plane/audit: add private upgrade/rollback event types + payload
control-plane/upgrade: emit audit events from API handlers and job runner
control-plane/upgrade: normalize version resolution (desired vs reported) for audit
tests: add audit sink assertions + redaction coverage
docs: update internal audit event catalog (private deployment section)
conversation: Marcus Lin (review): Can we guarantee the actor identity is stable for customer audit requirements? Specifically: if an installer uses an API token, do we log token id vs user id, and do we risk logging any secret material? Also please confirm automated rollback is clearly marked as system-triggered. Benji Okafor (author): Actor is derived from auth context: for user sessions we log user_id; for API tokens we log service_principal_id + token_name (not token value). No secret material is logged; redaction unit tests added and enforced in audit.Record. Automated rollback is actor_type=system with actor=redwood-control-plane and includes triggered_by_event_id pointing at the prior upgrade event. Ethan Park (review): Version fields — we should not trust installer-provided “from/to” strings. Please source from control-plane desired state + component version report endpoint, and document best-effort semantics. Benji Okafor (author): Updated to use version_resolver: to_version from desired upgrade target, from_version from the most recent component version snapshot; falls back to “unknown” if unavailable. Added comments in code and expanded tests for unknown cases. Allison Grant (review): For observability, can we include upgrade_correlation_id and request_id consistently? It will help correlate audit events with step logs from installer. Benji Okafor (author): Yes — request_id always present; upgrade_correlation_id included when the installer passes it (header) and we propagate into the job context. Added assertion in integration tests. Sean Gallagher (review): Failure_category mapping: ensure it’s bounded and doesn’t explode cardinality. Also, is emission ordering deterministic (started before completed) even under retries? Benji Okafor (author): Failure_category is a fixed enum; no raw error strings. For ordering: API emits started after enqueue; runner emits completed/aborted exactly once on terminal state. Retries won’t duplicate due to job terminal-state guard; added a test to ensure single terminal event. Marcus Lin (final): Approved after changes + redaction tests.
